mechanism_comparison.local_mechanism: Divisibility plus the digit ceiling turns a^K into at most Q(N+K); tail smallness then forces b^(N+K+1)<a(N+K). At a/b=3/2 this contradicts 2^(x+1)>3x for x>=2.
mechanism_comparison.integer_base_boundary: When b=1, the denominator-base exponential disappears; this is exactly why a literal integer-base intuition can look plausible before rational homogenization.
mechanism_comparison.published_rational_base_boundary: Bundschuh--Väänänen use a global analytic height condition rather than the local coordinatewise corridor, so their positive 7/2 theorem is not in tension with the no-go.
mechanism_comparison.exact_delta: A precise formal interface saying which local combination of divisibility and tail inequalities is impossible at 3/2.
